original.source: This manuscript constructs the one-loop quantum Batalin–Vilkovisky theory of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang–Mills theory on Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$, together with the transformations of its local operators under the whole superconformal algebra, in the renormalisation formalism of Costello [C07] and Costello–Gwilliam [CG2]. The single regulator is a lower cutoff $\varepsilon>0$ on Schwinger time; the upper end of every Schwinger integral is $\infty$, and no infrared scale and no dimensional continuation enter. This overview states what is constructed, where the construction needs care, how the chapters are organised, and the results of this first step.

The fields are those of ten-dimensional super Yang–Mills theory reduced to $\mathbb R^4$ [ESW, Prop 2.20, §10.3], complexified. Write $V$ for the complexification of $\mathbb R^4$ and $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$ for the six transverse directions, and $\mathfrak g$ for the complexified gauge Lie algebra with its invariant pairing $(-,-)$, which carries the coupling. The gauge field $A$ is a ten-component one-form with values in $\mathfrak g$: its components along $V$ form the connection $A|_V$, and its components $\iota_wA$, $w\in W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$, are the six scalars. The gaugino $\lambda$ takes values in the ten-dimensional semi-spin representation $\Sigma$, which in four dimensions is $S_+\otimes W\oplus S_-\otimes W^*$, with $S_\pm$ the two Weyl spinor representations and $W$ the four-dimensional R-symmetry space [ESW, §10]; spinors stay index free throughout. The ghost $c$ and the antifields $A^*$, $\lambda^*$, $c^*$ complete the fields [ESW, Def 3.2, Rem 1.36]. The action $S$ is [ESW, (31)] reduced to four dimensions; its quadratic part defines the linear differential $Q$, the rest is the interaction $I$, and $\{-,-\}$ is the odd Poisson bracket [C07, Lemma 4.3.2].

Costello's construction needs three more objects. A gauge-fixing operator $Q^{GF}$, here of Feynman type, makes $H=[Q,Q^{GF}]$ the Laplacian on every field. The heat kernel $K_t$ of $H$ at Schwinger time $t$ [C07, §6.5] gives the propagator

with $\partial_{P(\varepsilon,\infty)}$ the second-order operator contracting two fields with the kernel $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ [C07, §6.4]; this is the functional called $\Gamma$ in [C07, Def 6.6.1]. As in Theorem B of [C07], the counterterm $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ is the singular part of the graph expansion, extracted graph by graph, with coefficients in the span of $\varepsilon^{-1}$ and $\log\varepsilon$ at one loop; it is local, and $W\big(P(\varepsilon,\infty),I-I^{CT}[\varepsilon]\big)$ has a limit as $\varepsilon\to0$. A local operator $O$, for instance $\int\omega\,(\iota_{w_1}A,\iota_{w_2}A)$ with $\omega$ a compactly supported four-form [CG2, Lemma 10.1.1.3], enters through a square-zero parameter $\delta$ [CG2, Def 8.3.1.1]: the counterterm $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ of the family $I+\delta O$ defines the local operator at the UV end, $O(\varepsilon)=O-\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$, and its quantum observable is

The superconformal algebra $\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)$ [SW, (7), (17)] acts through an equivariant action $S+S^{(1)}+S^{(2)}$, a Maurer–Cartan element of the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex of [ESW, Def 1.26–1.27] with differential $d_{CE}$. Building $O[\infty]$ from the equivariant interaction, the transformation of $O$ along a generator $x_1\in\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)$ is the component $[(d_{CE}+Q)O[\infty]](x_1)$. Along the dilatation $\Delta$, the generator $2E$ of [SW, (17)] with $E$ the Euler vector field [SW, (3)], it is the anomalous dimension; along the supercharges $Q^i_\alpha$, $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha i}$ and the special supercharges $S^\alpha_i$, $\bar S^{\dot\alpha i}$ (the names of [SW, (8)]) it is the quantum-corrected supersymmetry; along the special conformal generators it is the primary condition. The program therefore has two outputs: the quantised interaction, with its counterterms and its quantum master equation, and, for every local operator, its observable and its transformations along all of $\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)$.

Operators. Inserting a composite operator produces divergences, and the limit defining $O[\infty]$ exists for many choices of the functional $O(\varepsilon)$. At scale $\infty$, however, $K_\infty=\lim_{t\to\infty}K_t=0$ on $\mathbb R^4$, and $P(0,\infty)$ is a contracting homotopy for $Q$: for compactly supported $\alpha$,

where $P(0,\infty)\star$ is the operator with kernel $P(0,\infty)$ [C07, §6.3]. Away from finitely many zero-mode classes, every $Q$-closed functional at scale $\infty$ without constant term is therefore $Q$-exact, and an arbitrary $O(\varepsilon)$ carries no cohomological information. The content of an operator is the locality of $O(\varepsilon)$: $O(\varepsilon)=O-\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ with local coefficients in the span of $\varepsilon^{-1}$ and $\log\varepsilon$. Locality and the existence of the limit fix the singular part uniquely, and the finite part is the scheme. An equation $[(d_{CE}+Q)O[\infty]](x_1)=Y[\infty]$ has content because $Y$ is required to be local, and anomalous dimensions are classes in the cohomology of local functionals.

Counterterms. Theorem B fixes the singular part $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ uniquely. The cutoff on every edge breaks gauge invariance and superconformal symmetry, and $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ contains $\varepsilon^{-1}$ mass terms with nonzero image under $Q$. The quantum master equation, transported to the UV boundary, then forces finite local counterterms. They are constrained by the master equation and fixed up to a choice; this choice is the renormalisation condition, part of the definition of the quantum theory and of every operator.

the second being [C07, Lemma 10.2.1] with $K_\infty=0$. Edges pinned at $t=\varepsilon$ and carrying $L_\varepsilon$ produce the singular coefficients and the scaling behaviour. Chapter 1 fixes the fields, the odd pairing, the reduced action with its linear differential and vertices, and the classical master equation. Chapter 2 realises $\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)$ on Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$ and constructs the equivariant action $S+S^{(1)}+S^{(2)}$ in the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex. Chapter 3 constructs the Feynman-gauge $Q^{GF}$, records which axioms of [C07, Def 4.3.3] it satisfies, and proves the UV-boundary identity, the acyclicity at scale $\infty$ and the one-loop formula. Chapter 4 computes the one-loop counterterms of the action in the two-, three- and four-point sectors and the quantum master equation at the UV boundary. Chapter 5 computes $O(\varepsilon)$ for the single letters and the scalar bilinears, Chapter 6 their dilatation through the scaling covariance of the regulator, and Chapter 7 the selection rules for the other superconformal components and the program of Steps 2–5.

This chapter fixes all three data for the reduction to Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$, writes the interaction vertex by vertex, and shows that the classical master equation determines the relative signs of the pairing.

The dilatation of a composite operator, and every other superconformal transformation, acts on the fields of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang–Mills theory up to gauge transformations and equations of motion. [ESW, (32)–(34), Thm 3.3] construct it for the Poincaré supersymmetry algebra; the special conformal transformations and the special supercharges require Weyl weights, a compensating term with the six scalars, and an R-symmetry rotation in the odd bracket. The dilatation is the simplest superconformal component of the BV transformation of an operator. The classical theory is invariant under the rescaling of the fields by their Weyl weights, and the regulator breaks this invariance through $\varepsilon$ alone: the rescaling maps $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ to $P(\lambda^2\varepsilon,\infty)$.
